lemma_reduction_separable.statement: Let A be a central simple k-algebra of degree p^2 over a field k of characteristic p. Then A is similar to a central division k-algebra D whose degree is 1, p, or p^2. If the degree of D is p^2, then D contains a maximal subfield L/k with [L:k]=p^2, and L/k is separable.
lemma_reduction_separable.proof: Proof. Let deg(A)=p^2. Step 1. By the Artin-Wedderburn structure theorem for central simple algebras, there exist a central division k-algebra D and an integer m>=1 such that A is isomorphic to M_m(D). Taking square roots of k-dimensions gives deg(A)=m deg(D). Since deg(A)=p^2 and p is prime, deg(D) is 1, p, or p^2. The fact that A is isomorphic to M_m(D) is precisely the statement that A and D are similar. Step 2. Assume now that deg(D)=p^2. We show that D contains a separable maximal subfield of degree p^2. We use the following standard facts. (F1) A central division k-algebra of degree n has maximal subfields, every maximal subfield has degree n, and every subfield has degree dividing n. This follows from Zorn's lemma and the double centralizer theorem. (F2) If E is a subfield of D with [E:k]=p, then the centralizer C=C_D(E) is a central division E-algebra of degree p. Indeed, C is a division algebra because the inverse of a nonzero element of C again commutes with E; the double centralizer theorem gives dim_k D = dim_k E * dim_k C, hence dim_k C = p^3 and dim_E C = p^2, so C has degree p over E, and its center is E. (F3) Every central division algebra of degree p over a field of characteristic p contains a separable maximal subfield of degree p. To justify F3, let B be such a division algebra over a field F. By the classical cyclic algebra theorem for prime degree (the Brauer class of a central simple algebra of prime degree p is represented by a cyclic algebra), B is a crossed product with a cyclic Galois extension L/F of degree p. In characteristic p, a cyclic extension of degree p is Artin-Schreier, so L=F(x) with x^p - x = a for some a in F. The polynomial T^p - T - a has derivative -1, hence is separable. The crossed product contains L as a subfield, and [L:F]=p, so L is a separable maximal subfield of B. Now let M be a maximal subfield of D; by F1, [M:k]=p^2. If M/k is separable, take L=M and we are done. Otherwise, let K0 be the maximal separable subextension of M over k. Since [M:k]=p^2, [K0:k] is either 1 or p. Case 1: [K0:k]=p. Put E=K0. Then E/k is separable of degree p. By F2, C=C_D(E) is a central division E-algebra of degree p. By F3, C contains a separable maximal subfield L/E of degree p. Then L is a subfield of D, [L:k]=p^2, and L/k is separable by the tower law for separable extensions. Case 2: [K0:k]=1. Then M/k is purely inseparable of degree p^2. We choose a subfield E0 of M of degree p over k. To see this, pick alpha in M not in k. Because M/k is purely inseparable of degree p^2, its exponent is at most 2, so alpha^(p^2) in k, and [k(alpha):k] is p or p^2. If [k(alpha):k]=p, set E0=k(alpha). If [k(alpha):k]=p^2, then alpha^p is not in k (otherwise k(alpha) would have degree at most p), and (alpha^p)^p=alpha^(p^2) is in k, so E0=k(alpha^p) has degree p over k. Thus E0/k is purely inseparable of degree p. By F2, C=C_D(E0) is a central division E0-algebra of degree p. By F3, C contains a separable maximal subfield L0/E0 of degree p. Then L0 is a subfield of D and [L0:k]=p^2. Since L0/E0 is separable and E0/k is purely inseparable, by multiplicativity of separable degree in towers the separable degree of L0 over k is p; equivalently, if K is the maximal separable subextension of L0 over k, then [K:k]=p. Thus K is a separable subfield of D of degree p. Now apply the argument of Case 1 with E=K (or directly F2 and F3) to obtain a subfield L of D with [L:k]=p^2 and L/k separable. By F1, any subfield of D of degree p^2 is maximal. This completes the proof.

lemma_similar_to_crossed_product_is_cros.statement: Let k be a field, let D be a central division k-algebra that is a crossed product, and let A be any central simple k-algebra similar to D. Then A is a crossed product, equivalently the Brauer class of A is represented by a crossed product division algebra.
lemma_similar_to_crossed_product_is_cros.proof: Let [X] denote the Brauer class of a central simple k-algebra X, and let Br(k) be the Brauer group. Recall the standard definition of similarity: two central simple k-algebras B and C are similar if B tensor_k C^op is split, i.e. isomorphic to M_m(k) for some m >= 1; when C is division this is equivalent to B being isomorphic to M_n(C) for some n >= 1. Since D is a central division k-algebra and A is similar to D, there exists m >= 1 such that A tensor_k D^op is isomorphic to M_m(k). The class of a split algebra is the identity 0 in Br(k), and the class of a tensor product is the sum of the classes. Also [D^op] = -[D]; for completeness, if deg D = d, the k-algebra map D tensor_k D^op -> End_k(D) sending a tensor b^op to the operator x -> a x b is nonzero, its kernel is a two-sided ideal of the central simple algebra D tensor_k D^op, hence is 0, and both sides have dimension d^4, so it is an isomorphism. Therefore D tensor_k D^op is isomorphic to End_k(D), which is isomorphic to M_{d^2}(k), so [D] + [D^op] = 0. Consequently 0 = [A tensor_k D^op] = [A] + [D^op] = [A] - [D], and thus [A] = [D]. By hypothesis D is a crossed product division algebra. Hence the Brauer class of A is represented by the crossed product division algebra D. To connect this with the phrase A is a crossed product, recall that a central simple algebra B is called a crossed product precisely when its Brauer class is represented by a crossed product division algebra; equivalently, there exists a crossed product division algebra E such that [B] = [E], and the last condition is exactly the statement that B is similar to E. Applying this to B = A and E = D shows that A is a crossed product. This also proves the asserted equivalent formulation: the Brauer class of A is represented by a crossed product division algebra, namely D. The argument covers all edge cases: if deg D = 1, then D = k is crossed product (take L = k and the trivial Galois group), and the same computation gives [A] = 0, so A is split and hence crossed product; if A = D, the conclusion is immediate.

lemma_crossed_product_p2_has_sep_p.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p and let D be a central division k-algebra of degree p^2. If D is a crossed product, then D contains a subfield E with [E:k]=p that is Galois over k (equivalently, separable over k).
lemma_crossed_product_p2_has_sep_p.proof: By the standard definition of a crossed product central simple algebra of degree p^2, D contains a subfield L such that L/k is Galois and [L:k]=p^2. Since deg D=p^2, L is a maximal subfield of D. Put G=Gal(L/k); then |G|=[L:k]=p^2. We first show that G has a normal subgroup H of order p. The center Z=Z(G) is nontrivial because the conjugation action of the finite p-group G on G has orbit sizes powers of p, so |G| is congruent to |Z| modulo p, and p divides |G|. If |Z|=p^2, then G is abelian. If |Z|=p, then G/Z is cyclic of order p; choosing a generator gZ, every element of G can be written as g^m z with z in Z, and two such elements commute because powers of g commute and elements of Z are central. Thus G would be abelian, forcing Z=G, a contradiction. Hence G is abelian. Now choose an element x not equal to the identity in G. If x has order p, set H to be the subgroup generated by x; if x has order p^2, set H to be the subgroup generated by x^p. In either case |H|=p, and H is normal because G is abelian. Let E=L^H be the fixed field of H in L. By the fundamental theorem of Galois theory, [E:k]=|G|/|H|=p. Since H is normal in G, E/k is Galois, with Gal(E/k) isomorphic to G/H of order p. In particular E/k is separable. Finally, E is contained in L and L is contained in D, so E is a subfield of D with [E:k]=p that is Galois over k, hence separable over k. This proves the lemma.
